sources.title: RFC 9293 — TCP Functional Specification
supports: three-way handshake and SYN sequence/ACK semantics

sources.title: RFC 6298 — Computing TCP's Retransmission Timer
supports: retransmit earliest unacknowledged segment after RTO
notes: Sections 2 and 5; actual on-wire retransmissions are environment-dependent

sources.title: Node.js — Net TCP API
supports: local stream-level fixture is not a packet trace
notes: Net Server and Socket events, Socket.end

claims.statement: A normal TCP active open synchronizes endpoint sequence spaces with SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK before the connection enters ESTABLISHED.
claims.rationale: RFC 9293 explicitly illustrates a basic three-way connection handshake with segment flags.

claims.statement: SYN consumes a sequence number, while an empty ACK does not advance its sender's TCP sequence space.
claims.rationale: RFC 9293 annotates SYN and subsequent ACK sequence/acknowledgment numbers.

claims.statement: TCP provides a reliable, ordered byte stream; a single application write does not establish a one-to-one on-wire segment boundary.
claims.rationale: RFC 9293 defines ordered sequence-number-based data delivery rather than application message framing.

claims.statement: TCP sender retransmissions can recover unacknowledged data; timeouts are not HTTP response status codes.
claims.locator: Section 3.8 Data Communication and Section 3.8.3 TCP Connection Failures
claims.rationale: RFC 9293 specifies retransmission and separate transport failure diagnostics.

claims.statement: On retransmission-timeout expiration the recommended RFC 6298 algorithm retransmits earliest unacknowledged data and doubles its RTO.
claims.rationale: RFC 6298 explicitly specifies RTO retransmission and exponential backoff.

claims.statement: TCP normal close uses FIN acknowledgments and supports half-closed directions; an abort can use RST instead.
claims.locator: Section 3.6 Closing a Connection and Section 3.6.1 Half-Closed Connections
claims.rationale: RFC 9293 defines normal FIN close and abort/reset as distinct transitions.

claims.statement: Node net Socket connect, data, end and error events expose application-level stream outcomes rather than decoded SYN/FIN/retransmitted packets.
claims.rationale: The official Node API defines these events and does not expose raw packet-flag evidence.
